tool_summary: Alpine Linux's package manager. Installs, upgrades, and removes system packages, typically requiring root, and runs arbitrary pre-install/post-install scripts. Especially relevant given how common Alpine-based images are as CI/container bases for agent-driven workflows.

rules.description: The --repository/-X flag adds or uses a repository other than those configured in /etc/apk/repositories. Installing from an untrusted or unfamiliar repository is a common supply-chain attack vector, since packages run arbitrary install scripts with root privileges at install time.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be removed, but its install-time scripts may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: The --allow-untrusted flag disables package signature verification entirely, removing the primary protection against tampered packages.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be removed, but its install-time scripts may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: Installs a package, running arbitrary pre-install/post-install scripts with root privileges at install time. Very commonly used in Dockerfiles and CI scripts targeting Alpine-based images.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be removed, but install-time scripts may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: Manages Alpine packages. Read-only subcommands (list, info, search) do not alter system state.
